messages:
Alice Kim: Heads-up — detection alert: our integration with CloudVector spiked 403/401 errors then a series of unusual POST requests that include long bearer tokens in query params. Suspect API key leakage. See snippet below.
InfraBot: [alert] 2026-03-20T09:12:03Z svc-cloudvector-integ: 403 x100, abnormal geodistribution, repeated from 3 IPs. Risk score 0.78. Related logs: `POST /cv/v1/upload?api_key=sk_live_XXX...`
Ben Jones: Can we immediately revoke the CloudVector service key? Which key is in use (svc account or org-level API key)?
Alice Kim: It's the service integration key stored in Secrets Manager under `secrets/cloudvector/primary`. Not a global org key but used by multiple services for ingestion.
Carla Morales: Agreed revoke now. Also enable short-term deny policy on the IAM role used by the integration. We'll need to rotate any KMS-wrapped keys if they were used to encrypt tokens.
Dave (SecOps): Taking action: 1) revoking current service key (in progress), 2) creating a temp deny on the integration role, 3) spinning up alternative ingest queue to drain/backfill. ETA 10m.
Emily Park (Vendor Ops): I'm opening a high-priority channel with CloudVector now. Asking for their latest deploys, access logs, and whether they rotated any keys. I'll ask for indicators of compromise and whether they saw any exfil from their side.
InfraBot: Revocation request submitted by Dave. API return: 200 revoke_ack. Traffic dropping but there are follow-on requests using the same token from different source IPs (likely replay).
Ben Jones: Good. Next: audit logs. Are we capturing KMS decrypt events and Secrets Manager read events for that secret? We need a timeline of who/what accessed it.
Carla Morales: Audit logs show SecretsManager:GetSecretValue at 2026-03-20T08:59:53Z from `svc-ingest-01`. KMS:Decrypt at 2026-03-20T08:59:54Z for key alias `alias/cloudvector-key`. Caller identity matches `svc-ingest-01` IP 10.3.4.21. Not seeing unexpected principals yet.
Dave (SecOps): Running a quick scan across infra for any other principals that used that secret. Also adding CloudTrail-style retention export to secure S3 bucket (read-only for secops).
Alice Kim: We should assume tokens in logs were exfiltrated. Who has access to CloudVector dashboards? Any shared links?
Emily Park (Vendor Ops): CloudVector confirms they rotated their ingest token at 09:00Z for a scheduled maintenance, but they also reported an internal bug that logged tokens to their request logs unintentionally between 08:50–09:05Z. They provided their logs and a list of IPs.
Ben Jones: If the vendor logged tokens, we need to check third-party storage. Do they ship logs to a cloud bucket or S3? If so, revoke read access and ask for evidence of deletion/retention policy.
Emily Park (Vendor Ops): They push logs to a customer-configured S3 prefix in our tenant. CloudVector says they set the wrong redaction flag, so tokens landed in logs. They've isolated the issue and will rotate on their side. Asking for timeline confirmation.
Carla Morales: Action items for us: 1) rotate service integration key (done by Dave), 2) generate new KMS CMK and re-encrypt secrets (planned), 3) search logs for any outgoing connections to the CloudVector IPs between 08:45–09:30Z, 4) run a quick exfil check for PII via our DLP rules.
Dave (SecOps): Key rotated at 09:22Z, new secret pushed to Secrets Manager with `version=v2`. Rolling deploy to all consumers in progress. KMS: created new key `arn:aws:kms:...:alias/cloudvector-key-v2`.
Ben Jones: Also check RBAC: any human users with broad access to Secrets Manager or S3 who could have pulled secret and put it somewhere else? We should tighten the principal list and add MFA required for secret operations.
Carla Morales: We have two users with SecretsManager full access: `ops-lead` (oncall) and `infra-admin` (platform). Both MFA-enabled. We'll audit their sessions; none showed access during the window except ops-lead for an unrelated task.
Alice Kim: Legal/comms — what's the customer impact? Did any customer data leave our environment?
Dave (SecOps): So far no evidence of PII exfil from our side. The leaked tokens were service API tokens used to POST data to CloudVector. If an attacker replayed requests, they could have ingested some payloads to CloudVector. We're pulling payload samples for the window and running pattern detection.
Emily Park (Vendor Ops): CloudVector confirms no public exfil visible but are doing deep scan. They've suspended log exports and will provide a signed attestation about retention and any downstream copies.
LegalBot: Please preserve all relevant logs and communications. Notify compliance lead within 2 hours. If customer data was forwarded outside for recipients not covered by our DPA, escalate to Legal for notification obligations.
Ben Jones: Contingency plan if CloudVector can't guarantee no exposure: 1) roll back to local fallback ingestion for affected customers, 2) rotate any downstream credentials that were used in that window, 3) commit to customer notification timeline (T+72 hours if required).
Carla Morales: Post-incident: schedule RCA, include vendor in postmortem, codify vendor redaction checks into onboarding checklist, add automated scans for tokens in outbound requests, and require vendor attestations for log redaction.
Alice Kim: Creating INCIDENT-2026-03-20-CLOUDVECTOR ticket and assigning owners: Dave (containment/keys), Carla (forensic + postmortem), Emily (vendor liaison + comms), Ben (remediation + infra hardening).
Dave (SecOps): Forensics update: preliminary payload scan found 2 POSTs containing base64-encoded blobs — investigating whether they include customer payloads.
InfraBot: Exported audit logs to secure bucket `s3://redwood-sec-archive/INCIDENT-1777777000/`. Read-only for secops, retention 365 days.
Ben Jones: Next steps: confirm final vendor attestation, finish payload scan, complete RBAC tightening and KMS rekey, and prepare a short customer-facing statement (if required).
Alice Kim: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in 60m with updates. Marking as P0. :lock:
